# AURA Stage 8.2 — Independent Verification Without AppWorld

**Decision date:** 25 October 2026  
**Status:** Research and experimental plan; no new external benchmark scores have been generated by this document.  
**Immediate decision:** Freeze the AppWorld infrastructure branch. Keep the v7 run (three authentic external agent tasks, all officially unsuccessful) as a negative baseline, but do not spend another Kaggle run repairing or optimizing it now.

## Why pivot

AURA is **Agent Uncertainty and Residue Arbiter**: an independent, contract-based verifier. It is designed to inspect postconditions, declared mutation boundaries, required process events, and evidence completeness, then issue `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `UNCERTAIN` with supporting evidence. Existing Stage 7 implementation has 186 regression tests and a preliminary Agent-Diff contract adapter. Stage 8.1 obtained four local LLM-driven workflows with four AURA/reference agreements; later AppWorld v7 produced three externally sourced agent trajectories, all unsuccessful under AppWorld's official grader, but **zero external AURA certificates**. These are separate evidence categories.

The scientific question is **not** whether Qwen can solve AppWorld. It is whether AURA can make *sound, cost-aware completion judgments* on unfamiliar agent tasks with explicit scope and trustworthy evidence, compared with strong baselines. The provisional novelty claim is narrow: obligation-aware counterexample-guided selection of additional evidence, with conservative certification and correctly reported total costs. Final-state checking, three-valued judgments, and error localization are prior art; do not claim them as original.

Published repository describes **1,000 trajectories** from HotpotQA, GAIA dev, BFCL and tau2 with step-level process labels. | **First, offline**: process/trusted-tool failure detection and appropriate abstention, no LLM inference necessary. | A transcript cannot certify persistent DB/file state. Separate process-only metrics. Verify files/labels/license locally before using. |
| **AgentRx (Microsoft)** | [Research](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/agentrx-diagnosing-ai-agent-failures-from-execution-trajectories/), [code](https://github.com/microsoft/AgentRx), [ACL 2026 paper](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-emnlp.598/). The October 2026 ACL abstract describes **170 annotated failed trajectories**; older Feb/Mar project material describes 115, reflecting an earlier version. | Additional independent failure-localization sample, compare kinds of trace-grounded failures and evidence. | Failure-only corpus cannot establish specificity/false-PASS performance on successful tasks; provenance/version freeze mandatory. Its objective is diagnosis, not completion certification. |
| **AgentSynth core_v2** | [GitHub](https://github.com/agentsynth/agentsynth). Maintainers describe **14 SQL-based workflow tasks**, readable outcomes, and deterministic mock/oracle policies. | **Second, stateful**: AURA must independently inspect before/after SQL state, all changes, and required trace/process events. Start with CPU-only oracle, no-op, and fault-injection *sanity* policies, then a real LLM on verified tasks. | Small, maintainer-authored pack, not an established peer-reviewed benchmark. | **AgentDojo (ETH Zurich, NeurIPS 2024)** | [Docs](https://agentdojo.spylab.ai/), [task-verifier interface](https://agentdojo.spylab.ai/api/base_tasks/), [code](https://github.com/ethz-spylab/agentdojo). ATFD [code](https://github.com/Galea-foo/atfd) is an optional benchmark of trajectory-monitoring tools with advertised 2,577 cases. Its mix of synthetic examples, programmatic and LLM-consensus labels makes it potentially useful as a secondary detector test, **not** primary independent state-certification evidence until dataset provenance and labels are inspected. Some sources have self-reported counts; counts are project statements, not results independently reproduced here.

## Immediate two-track experiment

### Track A — Offline execution-trace evidence, CPU only

1. Obtain the **version-pinned** AgentProcessBench data; hash inputs and record origin, license, number of episodes, and fields. No agent rerun needed.
2. Select a *preregistered* balanced subset covering successful/failed process steps and different source domains (if the supplied labels allow it). Do not pick cases after seeing AURA predictions.
3. Normalize original user request, tool schema, executed action, trusted tool return, step order, and recorded observations into a **read-only evidence adapter**. Record absent fields explicitly; do not synthesize missing states or tool successes.
4. Compile **human-reviewed process obligations from the task instruction and available tool/policy specification**, not from the answer labels. AURA `PASS` is allowed only for the stated *process-only contract* when sufficiently observed; otherwise `UNCERTAIN`. `FAIL` requires directly witnessed violation; a model's confident assertion alone is not trusted evidence.
5. Freeze contracts, run AURA and baselines, then reveal labels and compute **supported-process detection rate**, false accusations, uncertain/abstention rate, decisive coverage, and latency/evidence read counts. Report how many examples were unscorable because their reference labels involve semantic judgment or missing state.
6. Add AgentRx separately as a **failure-only** diagnostic subset; report failure recall and abstention, never balanced accuracy or specificity from negative-only cases. The current ACL paper says 170 cases while older materials cite 115: pin the exact release and verify count before reporting.

**Go/no-go:** At least 20 external readable trajectories from at least two domains with records sufficient for at least one independently checkable, explicit process obligation. If not, stop Track A and record why, rather than issuing unsound PASS verdicts.

### Track B — Real state evidence on external SQL workflows, CPU preflight

1. Pin AgentSynth source release, load 14 `core_v2` task definitions, and confirm the reference oracle/no-op policies and state fixtures work without model weights or API keys. Do not count these as external agent results.
2. For a first 5 tasks, define task-scoped contracts using the user goal and predeclared allowed mutation frame. **Reference oracle/expected outcomes must be hidden** until AURA predictions are frozen. Log any contract editing and annotator decisions.
3. Execute the official oracle, no-op, and clearly labeled injected-fault controls on separately reset world states. AURA independently probes the actual SQL database, compares the full declared mutation frame, and records trace evidence and probe costs. Required outputs: `pre_state`, `post_state`, `trusted_trace`, `contract`, `probe_observations`, `aura_certificate`, `native_reference`, hashes and noninterference receipts.
4. Only after this zero-GPU preflight works, run a **small genuine LLM agent** on the same 5 tasks with full documentation and enforced tool schema, then extend to the remaining pack. Compare performance with reference outcomes. Do **not** give the verifier the reference result as evidence.
5. Include examples with *satisfied desired state but unauthorized changes*, *tool says success but state unchanged*, *duplicate write*, *legitimate partial completion*, and *readback deliberately unavailable*. The fault-injected controls demonstrate sensitivity, not natural model failure rates.

**Go/no-go:** Actual persistent state available to independent probes; two oracle cases produce AURA `PASS` with complete mutation accounting; two known violations produce `FAIL`; one deliberately unreadable case produces defensible `UNCERTAIN` **unless a separate decisive violation is observed**; all judgments frozen before reference comparison. If these checks fail, debug only adapter/semantics, not the AI model.

### Track C — Stronger second source

If Track B works, select **20 preregistered ThinkingBox-Bench cases** spanning all five domains rather than 20 variations of one task family. Begin with dataset/import/correctness checks, then real agent execution. ThinkingBox's expected tool interactions are reference material only; keep them away from prompts and certification inputs. ToolSandbox remains a backup if ThinkingBox setup proves more complex than warranted.

## Pre-registered comparisons and outcome reporting

| Axis | Report (no fabricated score) | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Outcome soundness** | false PASS count, false FAIL count, UNCERTAIN count; stratify by missing state vs demonstrated violation | Wrong PASS is our highest-risk error |
| **Decisive coverage** | % episodes judged PASS/FAIL without unsafe guessing | An all-UNCERTAIN verifier is not useful |
| **Side effects** | true positive detection for out-of-frame persistent mutations, duplicate writes, required trace violations | AURA's residue/procedure claim |
| **Probe efficiency** | actual probe counts, I/O time, planner time, model time where applicable, full capture/setup cost | Stage 7 planner gains were cost-model-dependent |
| **Baselines** | native official evaluator (outcome reference), fixed exhaustive, cost-greedy, static/targeted, trace-only heuristic; matched evidence budgets | Prevent a straw-man victory |
| **Robustness** | clean run, partial write, silent no-op, repeated write, missing probe, stale or inconsistent record | Distinguish false evidence vs simply absent evidence |
| **Reproducibility** | exact source commit, task IDs, seeds, untouched official labels, run manifests, SHA256, tool versions, timestamps | Audit-ready results |

**Caveats:** Native evaluators usually produce binary task success. AURA is three-valued and often contract-scoped. State-based proof requires actual independent state; a text trajectory cannot prove absent side effects. Report contract coverage, label mismatch, and uncertainty separately; never force UNCERTAIN to FAIL just to inflate detector accuracy. No single 14-task pilot proves generality. Avoid selecting only failing agents or only one family. If oracle/reference logic itself has a bug, investigate and document it instead of assuming AURA is correct.

## What the team should do next (without another full Kaggle run)

**First:** Run the offline AgentProcessBench compatibility/access smoke (metadata, 20 cases, and a process-evidence adapter, no model) and the AgentSynth `core_v2` environment/oracle smoke in parallel. These are strictly preliminary access/sufficiency tests. **Second:** Commit to the one that exposes trustworthy evidence; run a small locked contract benchmark; report both negative and positive controls. **Third:** Expand only after collecting real external AURA certificates from stateful tasks.

**Do not** alter the published benchmarks to make AURA look better, train on the held-out expected outcomes, or replace missing evidence with LLM guesses. Preserve all Stage 8.1 files and make no GitHub commits without explicit approval.

## Candidate paper framing after genuine results

*Independent Evidence-Based Verification of Stateful AI-Agent Workflows: Soundness, Abstention, and Inspection Cost.*

This is an **experimental direction**, not yet a validated publication title or claim. Its defensible contribution must come from measured cost/error/coverage trade-offs of a concrete AURA system, not from asserting that independent state checking or three-valued logic is new.
